title: Thomas Conjecture (additive approximation of chromatic number)
statement_text: There exists $\alpha \geq 0$ with the following property: for every proper minor-closed class $\mathcal{G}$, there exists a polynomial-time algorithm taking as an input a graph $G \in \mathcal{G}$ and returning an integer $c$ such that $\chi(G) \leq c \leq \chi(G) + \alpha$.
context_text: Robin Thomas conjectured that the chromatic number of graphs in any proper minor-closed class can be approximated in polynomial time up to a constant additive error independent of the class (this is the affirmative answer to Question 2 of the paper). The conjecture was motivated by the analogous result for graphs embedded in a fixed surface, where additive error 2 suffices.
paper_contribution: Disproves the conjecture: unless P = NP, for every integer $k_0 \geq 1$ and every $1 \leq \beta \leq 4/3$, there is no polynomial-time algorithm to color a $K_{4k_0+1}$-minor-free graph $G$ using fewer than $\beta\chi(G) + (4 - 3\beta)k_0$ colors (Theorem 3 and Corollary 4).
notes: PDF source; statement reconstructed from Question 2 and the prose 'Thomas [15] conjectured that such a constant α exists'. No year inferrable from the extracted text.
paper_title: Additive non-approximability of chromatic number in proper minor-closed classes

title: Kawarabayashi et al. Conjecture (additive approximation for list coloring)
statement_text: There exists $\alpha \geq 0$ with the following property: for every proper minor-closed class $\mathcal{G}$, there exists a polynomial-time algorithm taking as an input a graph $G \in \mathcal{G}$ and returning an integer $c$ such that $\chi_{\ell}(G) \leq c \leq \chi_{\ell}(G) + \alpha$.
context_text: Kawarabayashi et al. conjectured that the additive approximability of chromatic number in proper minor-closed classes by a constant independent of the class holds even for list coloring. This strengthens the Thomas conjecture to the list-coloring setting.
paper_contribution: Disproves the conjecture as a consequence of Theorem 3 and Corollary 4; the non-approximability construction yields graphs for which no constant additive approximation of the list chromatic number is possible in polynomial time unless P = NP.
notes: PDF source; statement inferred from prose 'Kawarabayashi et al. [10] conjectured that this is the case even for list coloring'. The precise list-coloring formulation is reconstructed from context.
paper_title: Additive non-approximability of chromatic number in proper minor-closed classes

title: Open question: additive approximation for triangle-free graphs
statement_text: Does there exist $\alpha \geq 0$ such that for every proper minor-closed class $\mathcal{G}$, the chromatic number of triangle-free graphs in $\mathcal{G}$ can be approximated in polynomial time within additive error $\alpha$?
context_text: Approximating the chromatic number within additive error $\alpha$ on a class means a polynomial-time algorithm that, given $G$ in the class, returns an integer $c$ with $\chi(G)\le c\le\chi(G)+\alpha$. A graph $H$ is $t$-apex if deleting at most $t$ vertices makes it planar. Thomas conjectured, and Kawarabayashi et al. conjectured even for list coloring, that a single constant $\alpha$ works for every proper minor-closed class; the paper disproves this: for a $K_{4k_0+1}$-minor-free input, returning $c$ with $\chi(G)\le c\le\chi(G)+k_0-1$ is NP-hard. Its construction has clique number of order $k_0$. Forbidding triangles makes coloring more tractable for embedded graphs (all planar triangle-free graphs are 3-colorable by Grötzsch's theorem, and 3-colorability of triangle-free graphs on any fixed surface is decidable in linear time), and the authors explicitly state that the triangle-free version of the question is still open. On the negative side they show that forbidding $K_4$ is not sufficient: for $K_{4k_0+8}$-minor-free graphs with $\omega(G)\le 3$, additive error $d=\Omega(k_0^{1/4}/\log^{1/2}k_0)$ is NP-hard. On the positive side, for triangle-free $H$-minor-free graphs with $H$ $t$-apex they achieve additive error $\lceil(13t+172)/14\rceil$, and the answer is positive (with $\alpha=6$) for graphs of girth at least 5 in any proper minor-closed class.
notes: PDF source; stated in prose as 'this question is still open'.
paper_title: Additive non-approximability of chromatic number in proper minor-closed classes

title: Open question: better additive approximation for $K_{4k_0+1}$-minor-free graphs
statement_text: Is a better additive approximation of the chromatic number of $K_k$-minor-free graphs than the additive error $k-2$ of Kawarabayashi et al. possible in polynomial time (necessarily with additive error above roughly $k/4$, since for $k=4k_0+1$ additive error $k_0-1$ is NP-hard)?
context_text: Approximating the chromatic number of $K_k$-minor-free graphs within additive error $\alpha$ means a polynomial-time algorithm that, given a $K_k$-minor-free graph $G$, returns an integer $c$ with $\chi(G)\le c\le\chi(G)+\alpha$. Kawarabayashi et al. showed this is possible with $\alpha=k-2$. The paper shows that, unless P=NP, no polynomial-time algorithm takes a $K_{4k_0+1}$-minor-free graph $G$ and returns $c$ with $\chi(G)\le c\le\chi(G)+k_0-1$, so additive error about $k/4$ is impossible; this disproves conjectures of Thomas and of Kawarabayashi et al. that a constant additive error suffices for every proper minor-closed class. The authors leave open whether a better additive approximation than $k-2$ is possible, leaving a gap of roughly a factor of 4 between the algorithmic and hardness bounds. They also give, for $H$-minor-free graphs with $H$ $t$-apex (i.e. $H$ becomes planar after deleting at most $t$ vertices), an algorithm with additive error $t+3$.
notes: PDF source; stated in prose as 'We leave open the question whether a better additive approximation (of course above the bound ≈ k/4 given by Corollary 4) is possible'.
paper_title: Additive non-approximability of chromatic number in proper minor-closed classes
